InteractiveStuff documentation

Make held items react to the way you play. Learn the mod, configure its effects, and build your own first-person interactions with Vyn.

0.8.0Fabric · Client side0.8.0 feature set

Here to play?

Start with installation, try the bundled interactions, then tune the mod and pack settings.

Install InteractiveStuff →

Here to create?

Build a resource pack, transform a held model, and add particles, physics and player-facing options.

Create your first pack →

What the mod does

InteractiveStuff adds visual and sound interactions to held items. Its rendering hooks let resource packs replace or split models, move their parts, apply biome colors, simulate spring motion and draw first-person particles. The bundled InteractiveStuff resource pack supplies the ready-to-use effects.

The mod provides the engine and global controls. A resource pack provides scripts, models, textures and its own options. This distinction matters: disabling a pack effect does not disable the engine for other packs.

  • Bundled interactions: chests, pistons, an enchanting book, sculk sensors, note blocks, item physics, tints and more.
  • First-person particles: emitters, bursts, custom textures, lifetime curves and callbacks.
  • Physics library: spring motion driven by movement, looking around and optional wind.
  • Pack-defined settings: saved toggles, numbers, dropdowns, colors and text.

This offline guide covers the InteractiveStuff 0.8.0 feature set. Keyframe animation files and controls are documented separately in the 0.9.0 guide. Use the contents or search for an item, option or function. Expandable source listings and copy buttons work without a server.

Install & get started

#
  1. Install Fabric Loader for the Minecraft release you play.
  2. Download the matching InteractiveStuff 0.8.0 JAR and Fabric API. Put both in that instance’s mods folder.
  3. Optionally install the matching Mod Menu build. YACL is not required.
  4. Launch the client and check Options → Resource Packs. Keep the bundled InteractiveStuff pack enabled when you want its effects or import its libraries.
  5. Enter a world in first person. Try holding an enchanting table near a bookshelf, or crouch on a redstone block with a note block.

Install the mod on the client. Its held-item effects do not require a server installation and do not add server-side gameplay or physical world entities.

Open the settings

With Mod Menu installed, use Mods → InteractiveStuff → Configure. Without Mod Menu, use the InteractiveStuff button in Minecraft’s Options screen. A configurable settings keybind is also available under Controls; it starts unbound.

Match your Minecraft target

These are the minimum versions declared by this project’s current profiles, rather than a claim about the newest available releases. Use Fabric API and Mod Menu builds for the same Minecraft version. Optional Mod Menu builds may impose a higher Loader minimum of their own.

The render callback’s itemRendered is the actual current render model. Apply rendering changes to it there. The objects returned by player.getMainHandItem() and related getters are useful for inspecting stacks; changing one outside a rendering callback is not a persistent replacement for the active renderer.

Global objects

NameType / purpose
playerLocal Player wrapper
worldCurrent World wrapper
configInteractiveStuffConfig read-only access
keyKey translation helper
modLoaderInstalled mod, pack and game-version queries

Global functions

FunctionBehavior
importScript(packId, script)Execute an importable library in this script’s environment. The script name omits .vyn.
excludeScript(packId, script)Exclude the specified script from active callback dispatch.
debugText(text)Queue diagnostic text when the calling pack’s debug mode is enabled.
debugText(text, visible)Use an explicit boolean visibility flag, useful for a pack-owned counter switch.
translateText(key, ...arguments)Resolve a Minecraft language key to a displayed string, with optional format arguments.
getDelta()Frame duration normalized to 60 FPS: approximately 1 at 60 FPS. Paused frames use 0; the clock caps elapsed time at 50 ms (delta 3). It is not seconds or game ticks.
getFrameId()Monotonic frame identifier for preventing duplicate work in one render frame.
wait ticks do … endSchedule a block after a tick delay; this does not block the rest of the script. A nominal second is 20 ticks.

State lifetime

Top-level declarations run when a script loads; state persists between callbacks until reload/session reset. Scheduled work, model queues and particles are cleared when the session changes or scripts reload. A runtime error marks that script failed; check the game log, fix it and reload resources.

A render callback may run for both hands. Do not advance shared progress blindly in each call. Use getFrameId(), state keyed by logical hand and item ID, or the bundled smoothItemProgress helper. Logical main/off hand and physical left/right hand are different; prefer the appropriate ItemModel hand query.

Bundled item interactions

#

InteractiveStuff ships with a resource pack of Vyn scripts that add client-side, first-person item rendering effects. These examples are enabled with the bundled pack and can be configured in the resource-pack options.

EffectExamples
Animated item partsChest lids, pistons, vaults, redstone lamps, the enchanting-table book, sculk sensors, water buckets and extinguishing torches.
Item physicsMovement-driven motion for the mace, item frames, paintings and hanging signs, controlled by the pack physics options.
Particles and soundsEnchanting-table glyphs, sculk activation bursts, note-block notes and the note-block interaction sounds.
Color and appearanceBiome-aware tinting for foliage, saplings and water, plus the enchanting-table book display option.
Other item effectsTotem motion, item-model variants and helper functions shared by the bundled scripts.

The scripts live in assets/interactivestuff/scripts/ inside the bundled resource pack. You can inspect them as examples when creating your own Vyn resource pack.

Mod settings & navigation

#

InteractiveStuff has a built-in Minecraft-style settings screen; YACL is not required. Open it from InteractiveStuff in Mod Menu, from the Minecraft Options screen when Mod Menu is absent, or with the optional settings keybind.

Use the sidebar to switch categories, search to find a setting, and hover a control for its tooltip. Most changes are staged until you press Apply. Cancel discards the draft; reset and reload controls restore saved values. Hit-sound materials, excluded blocks and per-item pitch overrides use searchable inventory-style selectors.

Mod settings control the engine globally. Settings declared by a resource pack appear in the Packs area, grouped by pack and category, and are saved per pack. See Bundled resource-pack options.

Bundled resource-pack options

#

These controls belong to the bundled resource pack, rather than the mod's global engine settings. Open Packs, expand the bundled pack, then choose a category. Values are saved per resource pack.

CategoryOptions
AppearanceBlock, sapling and water tinting; showing the enchanting-table book.
PhysicsMaster physics switch; separate item-physics switches for the mace, item frames, paintings and hanging signs.
AnimationsShake intensity; pistons, chests, vaults, redstone lamps, enchanting books, sculk sensors, water-bucket animation and torch extinguishing.
ParticlesSeparate emission switches for enchanting tables, sculk sensors and note blocks.
SoundsNote-block sounds for crouching or swinging interactions.
DebugVyn debug text and particle counters.

Pack authors can declare their own options with ConfigOption; see Declare resource-pack settings.

Interactive hit sounds

#

Interactive hit sounds play a configured sound when a supported held item is swung. Configure them in the mod settings screen.

  1. Enable Interactive hits.
  2. Add or edit a material, then use the searchable item list to choose its items.
  3. Choose a registered sound and preview it before applying.
  4. Set volume, base pitch, random pitch and whether the swing must hit a block.
  5. Add per-item pitch overrides when a particular item needs a different pitch.
  6. Add excluded blocks when a block should suppress the hit sound.

Turning off Interactive hits disables the dependent hit-sound controls. Excluded blocks affect the sound response; they do not disable a resource pack's Vyn effects. The cooldown controls the ticks between hit sounds.

Create your first resource pack

#

Create a normal Minecraft resource pack with a pack.mcmeta, then add a script under the InteractiveStuff namespace:

MyPack/
  pack.mcmeta
  assets/
    interactivestuff/
      scripts/
        stick.vyn

A minimal script can target a held item and adjust its render model:

Enable the pack in Minecraft's Resource Packs screen. interactiveItems filters which held items receive onItemUpdate; other events require their own item checks. Continue with Vyn language essentials and Models, transforms & colors.

Vyn language essentials

#

Vyn is the scripting language used by InteractiveStuff resource packs. Scripts are loaded from assets/interactivestuff/scripts/. Use make for a value that can be reassigned and lock for a value that should stay fixed. A task declares reusable code or an event callback.

Use check condition do ... end for a condition and otherwise for its alternate branch. Use reply value to return from a task. Lists and maps provide collections; new Type(...) constructs exposed Java-backed Vyn objects. importScript(packId, scriptName) loads a helper script from a resource pack. For the full language grammar and expressions, consult the Vyn documentation.

Events, globals & timing

#
Event taskWhen it runsCommon use
task onTick doEach active client game tick while the world is ready and unpaused.Timers, state updates and checks that do not need to run every render.
task onItemUpdate takes itemRendered doFor each matching held item render.Transforms, replacement models and particle emitters. The argument is the current render model.
task onSwingHand doWhen the local hand-swing callback fires.React to a swing; check the held item yourself when needed.
task onPlaySound takes sound doWhen the client observes a sound notification.Inspect its ID, pitch, volume or position. Avoid recursively responding to a sound your script plays.
task onKeyPress takes keyInput doFor a gameplay key press when no screen is open.Compare the integer key code; this is not a text-character event.

Global objects

GlobalPurpose
playerLocal player state, held stacks, movement and block queries.
worldWorld state, block and biome queries.
configRead-only access to mod configuration values.
modLoaderInstalled mod, selected resource-pack and game-version queries.
particlesSession particle counts and particle clearing.
keyLegacy translation helper; prefer translateText for displayed text.

Use onTick for gameplay-tick state and onItemUpdate for render-local changes. Event tasks are callbacks, not ordinary functions you call manually. For particles, declare emitters once and bind them during the relevant render callback; see First-person particles.

Models, transforms & colors

#

Replace a model or add a part

itemRendered.setItemModel(id) replaces the appearance of the current rendered stack. new ItemModel(itemId) and itemRendered.copy() enqueue an additional model for that render; they are useful for lids, pages and overlays. Use the current model when you want replacement.

Translations, pivots and particle anchors use render/model units, not screen pixels. Model JSON element coordinates are normally expressed on a 0–16 grid, while these render coordinates use unit-scale values; the first-person display transform also affects the final position. Rotations take degrees. Scaling multiplies the model’s scale; shear takes six cross-axis factors.

Pivot & parenting

setPivot(x,y,z) controls the transform anchor. A parent supplies its transform and inherited light/glint where not overridden. Self-parenting and cycles are rejected. detach() removes the parent relationship. Use the pivot marker tools to place hinges in both physical hands.

Turn toward a world position

lookAt(position) aims at a block center. The overload lookAt(position, group, speed, weight) smooths a shared group’s orientation; use the same group for cooperating parts. Speed and weight must be 0–1, and the group must be nonempty, at most 80 characters. setLookAtClearance(surface,minX,minY,minZ,maxX,maxY,maxZ) supplies a clearance plane and local bounds for that aiming path; it is not general collision physics.

Which color function?

FunctionAffects
setTint(index, packedColor)Only model faces with the requested tint index. Prefer this for grass, foliage and water masks.
setTint(packedColor)The fallback tint override, stored at index −1; it can recolor untinted faces as well. Use the indexed overload to preserve dirt or wood.
setColor(r,g,b)The model’s RGB multiplier. Use 0–255 channels.
setQuadColor(packedColor)A selection-color override applied through the selected quad path.
setOpacity(value)Opacity multiplier, clamped to 0–1.

Use the right resolver: world.getGrassColor(position), getFoliageColor, getDryFoliageColor or getWaterColor. They return packed colors for setTint. The model must have suitable tintindex faces. For RGB/ARGB integers with no alpha bits, the tint setter supplies opaque alpha.

Quad selection

setQuads(start,end) sets the affected half-open range; unselected geometry remains visible unless exclusive selection is used. The end index is excluded; an end of 0 means the full layer. select(start,end) also enables exclusive selection. Quad ordering depends on the baked model and version, so a range is not a stable identifier for a named model part.

Custom assets across versions

Legacy model routing and modern item-model definitions differ by Minecraft target. Inspect the bundled models and version adapters before distributing a cross-version pack; do not assume one modern item-definition JSON works on 1.20.1. Data-component operations also depend on each target’s supported component bridge.

Bundled chest parts now load Minecraft’s chest images through block-atlas sprite aliases, so active resource-pack replacements of minecraft:textures/entity/chest/*.png are used. Edited sapling masks, bucket water and extinguished-torch images remain pack assets because they are effect-specific.

First-person particles

#

A ParticleEmitter is a persistent Vyn object. Declare it once at script load, configure it, and attach it to the current model inside onItemUpdate. It owns separate channels for the two logical hands.

These are custom first-person billboards. They use vanilla particle appearances or custom PNGs, but they do not instantiate Minecraft’s native world-particle behaviors. Choosing minecraft:enchant, for example, chooses its textures; you still define its motion.

Coordinate spaces

SpaceAfter spawningUse
itemPositions continue to follow the attached model’s transform.Glows or particles that move with the item.
viewThe spawn anchor is applied once; particles remain in view coordinates as the player moves/turns. This is the default.Screen-relative first-person flourishes.
worldThe spawn anchor is converted to world coordinates once; camera motion changes their projection.Particles that appear to remain behind when you walk or turn.

setAttached(true) is the older shortcut for item space; setAttached(false) selects view space. Use setSpace("world") explicitly for world-relative behavior. In world space, callback positions and spawn positions are world coordinates; in item space they are local coordinates. Initial velocity is transformed by the spawn anchor in detached spaces.

Timing, spread & motion

  • Rate is particles per game tick, per active hand. 0.05 is about one particle per second per hand at 20 TPS and 100% density.
  • Lifetime, lifetime spread and animation frame duration use ticks. Lifetime is at least one tick.
  • Spread is independently randomized at each birth from −amount to +amount on each axis. Use it for randomized emitter offsets instead of calling random once at load.
  • Velocity is displacement per tick in the relevant coordinate space. Velocity spread independently randomizes those components.
  • Gravity subtracts from Y velocity each tick. Negative gravity rises. Drag multiplies velocity by 1 − drag, after gravity.

Lifetime curves & easing

Size, opacity, color and billboard rotation support start/end curves and extra keyframes. Progress is normalized from 0 to 1. A key’s easing controls the interval arriving at that key. Set the start/end curve before adding intermediate keys.

Supported families: linear, step, quad, cubic, quart, quint, sine, expo, circ, back, bounce and elastic. Use the in, out and inOut prefixes; an optional ease prefix and hyphens/underscores are accepted. For example, easeOutCubic starts fast and slows near the end.

A mathematical illustration of the easing curve, rather than a Minecraft rendering preview. Back easing can overshoot.

Textures & frame lists

setType("minecraft:smoke") reads the active resource pack’s assets/minecraft/particles/smoke.json texture list. A custom type can supply the same JSON shape in its own namespace. Each texture entry resolves under textures/particle/.

Store those frames as assets/mypack/textures/particle/spark_0.png and so on. Then call setType("mypack:spark"). Or bypass the frame list with setTexture("mypack:textures/particle/spark.png") for one PNG. Calling setType again clears a direct-texture override.

Animation modeBehavior
lifetimeDistribute the texture-list frames over the particle’s lifetime. Default mode.
loopAdvance and loop using the specified frame duration in ticks.
randomChoose one list entry for each particle and keep it.
firstAlways use the first list entry.

Choose with setAnimation(mode, frameTicks). The duration must be 0.05–12000 ticks, even for modes that do not use it. A frame list may contain at most 256 textures. A missing type or list falls back to a generic appearance and logs a warning; direct textures should always point to an existing PNG.

Visibility, lifecycle & limits

Depth testing defaults on: setDepthTest(false) draws an effect without the normal depth test. setLight(-1) inherits item light; 0–15 forces brightness. World space does not add collision, world lighting simulation, multiplayer visibility or third-person rendering.

stop() stops new births and clears pending bursts; living particles finish naturally. clear() removes an emitter’s living particles and pending work without changing its enabled state. Item changes finish naturally by default; setClearOnItemChange(true) removes them immediately instead. Changing emitter properties affects newly born particles; an existing particle keeps its birth settings unless its callback changes it.

The engine permits up to 256 emitters per session, up to 128 queued burst births per hand, and up to 128 births per hand per tick. Emission rate is 0–64 per tick. Global density and the 0–4096 particle cap still apply to bursts. Use particles.getDroppedCount() to inspect births dropped at the active-particle cap.

Particle recipes & callbacks

#

Burst once when an action happens

Continuous emission defaults to zero. Keep the rate at zero and request a burst from an event, not every render frame. This example emits from a held stick on a swing.

burst(count) queues both channels; births require an attached, active held item. If both hands hold the filtered item, both can emit. Use burstForHand(true,count) for logical main hand or burstForHand(false,count) for off hand. emit() is a one-particle burst. A stopped emitter must be started before queued births can occur.

Ease a rise and set color per particle

There is no setVelocityOverLife function. For an exact fast-to-slow rise, calculate a position curve from the particle’s progress. Put these tasks in the same script as the emitter.

Use setOnSpawn("taskName"), setOnUpdate("taskName") and setOnDeath("taskName"). Each task receives a Particle. Update runs after the engine’s motion/lifetime step while the particle is alive. Death callbacks run for normal tick-driven removals; bulk clear(), reload and global disabling are cleanup operations and do not promise a death callback for every particle.

For pitch-based colors, calculate RGB in the spawn callback from the pitch used for that note. The bundled note_block.vyn includes an example using a normalized 0.5–2.0 pitch and three phase-shifted sine functions.

Fresh random offsets on every birth

Each new particle receives a fresh X/Z offset around the center. Use a spawn callback with random() when you need a non-box distribution. setSeed(integer) makes an emitter’s random sequence repeatable for testing.

Physics library

#

The bundled physics_lib.vyn is an importable spring simulation, rather than a rigid-body or collision engine. It produces angleX and angleZ for the calling script to apply to a model. Movement, changes in camera input and synthetic wind feed the springs.

runPhysicsEngine(stiffness, damping, moveRes, lookRes, vertRes, inertial, maxAngle, windMult)

ParameterMeaning
stiffnessRestoring spring force. Increase it for a quicker return to rest.
dampingResistance to angular velocity. Increase it to settle oscillation sooner.
moveResResponse to changes in horizontal player velocity. A negative value reverses its direction.
lookResResponse to changes in the camera pitch/yaw input values.
vertResResponse to changes in vertical player velocity.
inertialMultiplies movement/look impulses and synthetic wind force. Larger values increase those forces; this is not a physical mass in kilograms.
maxAngleClamp in degrees on both output axes; the boundary partially reflects angular velocity.
windMultStrength of time-varying synthetic wind. Zero disables it; it is not Minecraft weather.

The example’s values are an illustrative starting point, not enforced ranges. The library steps at most once per render frame in each importing script environment. It resets after a rendering gap or significant time interruption and subdivides integration steps. If two items in the same script call it with different settings in one frame, the first call chooses that frame’s parameters.

State & the master switch

The imported library declares its own physics_enabled pack option and resets when that value changes. resetPhysicsEngine() clears angles, velocities and timing state. Importing into separate scripts gives them separate state; the library does not automatically create an independent spring for every model part.

Movement values are already adapted

player.getVelocityX/Y/Z() return motion transformed into the player’s horizontal yaw frame and scaled by approximately one third. The Y getter removes a small resting gravity offset. Treat them as animation inputs, not unscaled world-space blocks per tick. In the library, the Z input is negated before calculating impulses.

Shake versus spring motion

The pack’s Shake intensity scales random jitter in totems, sculk, torches and maces. Physics switches control the spring behavior of frames, paintings, hanging signs and maces. Shake at 0% does not turn off all spring sway; the master physics switch does not suppress unrelated random jitter.

The bundled effect_helpers library also exposes createProgressState(), smoothItemProgress(state,item,target,speed), resetItemProgress(state,item), packToggle(id,category), packShakeOption(), hasMod(id) and isRedstonePowered(). These are pack library tasks, not built-in globals.

Declare resource-pack settings

#

Create a ConfigOption at the top level of a script. The mod registers it under the real owning pack, displays it in Packs and stores the player’s value separately from your declaration. Read its value during callbacks to control an effect.

Available types

TypeDefault valueConfigurationReader
toggletrue / falseLabel, tooltip, category, callbackgetBoolean()
numberFinite numbersetRange(min,max,step)getNumber()
dropdownOne of the choice stringssetChoices(["a","b"])getText()
color"#RRGGBB"Six hexadecimal RGB digitsgetColor() / getRed/Green/Blue()
textStringsetMaxLength(length)getText()

Declaration rules

  • Constructors and schema setters are only valid during script loading. Do not create settings in onTick, a particle callback or a render event.
  • IDs use 1–96 letters, digits, dots, hyphens or underscores. Keep them stable when updating a pack.
  • Duplicate declarations in the same pack must agree on their normalized schema. Reusing an ID with a different type/default/range is an error.
  • Numbers require finite min < max and 0 < step ≤ max − min. Values snap to the step and clamp to the range. The default range is 0–1 with step 0.01, so set a range for values such as 20.
  • Dropdowns require 1–64 choices; the default must be a listed choice. Text defaults to a maximum of 256 characters; the allowed maximum is 1–4096.
  • Labels allow 160 characters, tooltips 1024, category names 96, callback task names 160. Strings may be literal text or resolvable language keys.

Apply, callbacks & persistence

setOnChange("taskName") registers a task called with (option, previous, value) when a committed value changes. Editing a draft or cancelling does not call it. Use callbacks to stop emitters or reset progress, while ordinary rendering callbacks read the current saved value.

Player values are saved globally per resource pack in config/interactivestuff.json. Reloading a pack rebuilds declarations without deliberately overwriting its saved choices. Renaming the pack’s actual folder/ZIP identity can give it a different saved-settings namespace.

Localized labels

Use a translation key in setLabel, setTooltip or setCategory, and provide that key in assets/<namespace>/lang/en_us.json. translateText is the preferred helper when you need the resolved string inside Vyn.

Debugging & performance

#

Find your model anchors

Enable Debug → Pivot markers and call setPivot in the script. Purple/violet diamonds identify main/off-hand pivots. Enable Emitter markers for green/orange crosses at emitter origins. The symbols distinguish them even when their colors are hard to tell apart.

Markers through items shows markers over the held model. Turn it off to test whether a point is actually hidden by the model’s surface. This is a diagnostic visibility option; it does not alter particle depth settings. Pivot markers do not require particles to be enabled.

Pack-controlled text

The bundled pack supplies Vyn debug text and particle counters under its own Debug category. A custom pack can declare independent options and use the explicit visibility form:

Keep rendering light

  • Declare settings and emitters once at load, rather than every frame.
  • Use interactiveItems to avoid dispatching a script for irrelevant items.
  • Keep broad block searches out of render loops where possible. hasNearbyBlock and getNearestBlock cache queries by tick and player block position; nearest search accepts a radius up to 32.
  • Use low rates and reasonable lifetimes. At steady state, a rough budget is rate × lifetime × active hands × density multiplier.
  • Use built-in lifetime curves instead of per-particle update tasks when a curve is sufficient.
  • Avoid calling burst() each render frame for a one-shot event.
  • Check both physical hands and different GUI/FOV/resource-pack combinations before distributing a pack.

Script failures include the owning pack/script and phase in logs/latest.log. Reload resources after correcting a failed script. An error can disable just the failing script, so a partly working pack can still have a load or callback failure.

ItemModel

#

Model rendering, stack information, transforms, tint, lighting, parts and targeting.

Use the render callback’s itemRendered, or create an extra model with new ItemModel(itemId).

61 exposed signatures. Return types retain their source names: int/long/float/double are numeric values; void is shown as nothing.

setDrag(double drag)nothingSet velocity damping 0–1; each tick multiplies velocity by 1 − drag. Default 0.

There is no active Christmas chest model in the current pack.

Troubleshooting

#

No settings button in Options

If Mod Menu is installed, the separate Options entry is intentionally hidden. Open the mod’s Configure screen from Mod Menu, or assign the optional settings keybind.

A script never runs

Check the enabled pack, the exact assets/interactivestuff/scripts/ path, the .vyn extension and latest.log. Check interactiveItems against the actual held item ID. Reload with F3+T after changes.

A library import fails

Use the real pack ID, include file/ for local folder/ZIP packs, omit .vyn from the script name, and keep the providing pack enabled. Imported libraries must not define automatic event tasks.

A setting does not appear

Declare ConfigOption and call its schema setters at load time, not inside an event. Check for conflicting duplicate schemas, invalid defaults or a missing callback task. Then reload resources.

A model appears twice

new ItemModel and copy enqueue additional models. To replace the current held appearance, call setItemModel on itemRendered in its render event.

Grass dirt is tinted too

Use setTint(0, world.getGrassColor(position)) on a model whose grass faces have tintindex 0. A whole-model RGB multiplier also colors the dirt.

Foliage is gray or the color is wrong

Check the pack’s tint option, global Color changes, tint indices, and whether the script uses the foliage resolver. Confirm you are using the correct target JAR and active custom model. The global getBiomeColorAt alias means foliage, not all color types.

Particles move with the camera

Use setSpace("world") if particles should stay where they were born. setAttached(false) selects view space instead.

Particles keep emitting

Use setRate(0) plus a burst in the action event. A burst inside onItemUpdate will repeat every render frame. stop stops births; clear removes already living particles.

No particles are visible

Check the global particle switch/density/cap, the pack emission switch, first-person view, emitter enabled state and per-frame attach. Confirm its item filter and texture path. The enchanting effect also needs a visible animated book and a nearby bookshelf.

A burst has fewer particles than requested

Global density scales bursts too, the active cap can drop births, pending counts clamp to 128 per hand, and only attached active hands can spawn.

Motion is faster with two held items

Store progress per logical hand and item, or guard simulation with getFrameId. Repeatedly updating one global number in both render calls advances it twice.

A key callback does not fire

onKeyPress is for gameplay key input while no screen is open. Check the integer key code. It is not a GUI character-typing hook.

A modern data component fails on 1.20.1

That target uses a limited legacy mapping. Unsupported modern component IDs are rejected; use a supported legacy key/nbt:TagName and test the target.

Punchy or another first-person renderer changes behavior

Some rendering mods bypass vanilla render paths, and bundled scripts also have explicit installed-mod checks. Partial visual overlap is not proof of full compatibility. Test the matching target and toggles; consult the scripts before combining effects.

Multi-version project & Gradle

#

The repository is an all-in-one Gradle project. Open its root in the IDE. Shared production code and resources live in src/main/; version-specific adapters live in versions/<profile>/src/. A version override with the same path wins over the inherited file, so a root edit reaches every target that does not override it.

The profile chain is defined in the version properties. The 26.1 patch modules reuse the 26.1.X profile with their own patch dependencies. Treat generated files in build/ as outputs; edit the source roots instead.

MinecraftBuildRun clientGenerate IDE game sources
1.20.1build1_20_1run1_20_1sources1_20_1
1.21.1build1_21_1run1_21_1sources1_21_1
1.21.5build1_21_5run1_21_5sources1_21_5
1.21.10build1_21_10run1_21_10sources1_21_10
1.21.11build1_21_11run1_21_11sources1_21_11
26.1build26_1run26_1sources26_1
26.1.1build26_1_1run26_1_1sources26_1_1
26.1.2build26_1_2run26_1_2sources26_1_2
26.2build26_2run26_2sources26_2
26.3build26_3run26_3sources26_3

Per-target tasks also work with qualified paths, such as ./gradlew :1.20.1:build. Windows users can use gradlew.bat in place of ./gradlew.

Outputs & checks

releaseAll collects the ten checked release JARs and checksums into build/dist/0.8.0/ and creates build/dist/InteractiveStuff-0.8.0-all-versions.zip. It does not publish. Local developer docs/tests are excluded from the mod JARs and release ZIP.

Where local client-test fixtures are present, testAll or a version task such as test26_3 runs graphical client checks sequentially and needs a display. Those fixtures were deliberately kept local and are not a promise that a fresh public checkout includes every local test source. Ordinary build/check tasks include the checks available to that checkout.

Publishing commands

previewPublish prepares a dry-run plan. publishAll performs real uploads to configured Modrinth/CurseForge projects with credentials; run it only when you intend to release. It reads root changelog.md by default, or -Pchangelog_file=/path/to/notes.md. The full changelog goes on 26.3 by default; other uploads contain a short reference. -Pchangelog_target changes the full-notes target.

Publishing settings include release_type (release/beta/alpha), publish_platforms and publish_dry_run=true. Credentials use MODRINTH_TOKEN and CURSEFORGE_TOKEN from the environment or private Gradle properties. This documentation build performs no uploads.

About this reference

#

Prepared for InteractiveStuff 0.8.0 from the local source on 30 October 2026. The original wiki provided the type-by-type organization; current annotations, implementations, settings schemas and bundled scripts determined the API and feature coverage.

  • InteractiveStuff repository
  • Original InteractiveStuff wiki
  • Vyn language repository
  • Modrinth project
  • CurseForge project

This file embeds its styles, scripts, mod icon and reading fonts. No CDN, network fetch, account or installation is needed to read it. External source/download links naturally require a connection. You can print it or save it as PDF through your browser.

InteractiveStuff by OmarDotContent. Mod artwork is the project’s existing icon. Embedded Noto Sans / Noto Sans Display fonts are by the Noto project, licensed under the SIL Open Font License 1.1; the license is included in this file. Minecraft names describe integration with Minecraft Java Edition; this is community documentation.
